verdict_reasoning: One objection survived, already-exists-1, and it is a fixable question of value against cost. Message #1 says `alter table ... rename constraint` already works on foreign tables, so the new form is a second spelling. It matches the existing rename column and add/drop constraint forms and reuses the existing rename path. The three command tag objections were refuted, so nothing that survived stops the proposal at levels 1-2.

brief.title: Add alter foreign table ... rename constraint
brief.problem: alter foreign table can add and drop constraints but cannot rename them, while alter table can. The author calls this an inconsistency that users of foreign tables hit. alter table ... rename constraint already works on foreign tables, but users do not easily find this.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds a RENAME CONSTRAINT form to the alter foreign table grammar and reuses the existing rename path. It refactors AlterObjectTypeCommandTag() so that column and constraint operations return the command tag ALTER FOREIGN TABLE or ALTER TABLE, matching the command used. It also extends psql tab completion.
user_visible_surface: New syntax: alter foreign table [ if exists ] [ only ] name [ * ] rename constraint old to new.
Command tag for column or constraint operations now follows the command used (ALTER TABLE or ALTER FOREIGN TABLE).
psql tab completion for alter foreign table rename constraint, and for add/drop column/constraint.
author_claims: The feature is niche, but the author hit it while working intensively with foreign tables.
The code change is fairly small.
No reason exists not to support it, and alter foreign table already has non-standard extensions.
It makes alter foreign table consistent with alter table, as with owner to.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. No one has replied, and the CommitFest entry is in Needs review for version 20.
unclear: The material does not say which constraint types foreign tables can carry, so it does not say which ones this form can rename.
The patch does not say whether command tags change for any existing command, which may affect event triggers or clients that read tags.
The material does not say how [ * ] and only behave for inherited constraints on foreign tables.
The material does not say whether the regression tests cover the command tag change.
search_queries: psql tab completion alter foreign table

objections.title: Rename constraint on foreign tables already works through alter table
objections.failure_scenario: A user today runs `alter table ft_foo rename constraint alice to bob` and gets exactly the result the new syntax gives. The patch adds a second spelling, plus a command tag refactor in utility.c. If that refactor changes the tag of any existing column or constraint command, event triggers or tools that filter on the tag can stop matching after an upgrade.
objections.argument: Message #1 states that alter table ... rename constraint works on all table-like objects, so the gap is that users cannot find it, not that the job cannot be done. A documentation cross-reference in alter_foreign_table.sgml would cover the same need without grammar or command tag changes. The author's consistency case is real, since alter foreign table already has rename column and add/drop constraint. Still, [P1] shows a small ease-of-use gain being weighed against even modest added code.
objections.author_must_show: Why is a cross-reference to alter table rename constraint in the alter foreign table docs not enough, and does the tag refactor change the tag of any existing command?

precedents.title: [PROPOSAL] : Disallow use of empty column name in (column_name '') in ALTER or CREATE of foreign table.

critic.reasoning: Message #1 confirms that `alter table ... rename constraint` already does the job and calls the need niche, so the documentation-only alternative needs an answer. [P1] concerns an option validator and gives weak support, and the tag-change part of the scenario has no basis in the material.

refuted.title: Command tag change for existing alter foreign table rename column
refuted.failure_scenario: A site runs an event trigger defined with `when tag in ('ALTER TABLE')` that audits column renames. After upgrade, `alter foreign table ft rename column a to b` reports the tag ALTER FOREIGN TABLE, so the trigger no longer fires. The site finds out when audit records for foreign tables stop appearing.
refuted.argument: The commit message says the patch refactors AlterObjectTypeCommandTag() so that column and constraint operations return the tag of the command used. The rename path today chooses its tag by object type, so an existing command such as alter foreign table ... rename column probably changes its reported tag as a side effect. Event triggers filter on tags, and clients log them, so this changes behaviour for existing users who did not ask for it. The proposal treats the change as plumbing and does not mention any user-visible effect or a release note.
refuted.author_must_show: Which existing commands report a different command tag after this patch, and should that change be a separate, release-noted commit with tests for event trigger tag filtering?

critic.reasoning: Postgres today takes the tag for a column rename from the relation type named in the command, so `alter foreign table ... rename column` already reports ALTER FOREIGN TABLE. The trigger in the scenario does not fire for that command before the patch either.

refuted.title: Command tag change for existing commands is not stated or bounded
refuted.failure_scenario: An admin has an event trigger declared with `when tag in ('ALTER TABLE')` that audits column renames, including renames on foreign tables. After upgrading to a release with this patch, `alter foreign table ft rename column a to b` may report ALTER FOREIGN TABLE instead. The trigger then stops firing and nothing reports an error, so the gap shows up only when someone checks the audit log.
refuted.argument: The commit message says AlterObjectTypeCommandTag() was refactored so that column and constraint operations return the tag that matches the command used. That suggests at least one existing command form returns a different tag today. Event trigger tag filters are stored in pg_event_trigger and survive pg_upgrade, and clients and poolers read the tag from CommandComplete. Message #1 does not list which existing forms change their tag, and the patch prose does not say so either.
refuted.author_must_show: Which existing statements return a different command tag after this patch, and will event triggers filtered on the old tag still fire for them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, and it rests on the same scenario. `alter foreign table ... rename column` already reports ALTER FOREIGN TABLE, so the material shows no existing command whose tag changes.

refuted.title: Command tag change for existing commands is bundled with new syntax
refuted.failure_scenario: A site has an event trigger with `when tag in ('ALTER TABLE')` that audits column renames. After upgrade, `alter foreign table ft rename column a to b` may report ALTER FOREIGN TABLE, so the trigger stops firing. The site finds out when audit rows go missing.
refuted.argument: The commit message says AlterObjectTypeCommandTag() is refactored so that column and constraint operations return a tag that follows the command used. That likely changes the tag of `alter foreign table ... rename column`, which works today, not only the new form. Event triggers, pg_stat_statements users and tools that parse tags see this. The proposal treats it as a side detail and does not list it as a behaviour change or offer it as a separate patch.
refuted.author_must_show: Which existing commands return a different command tag after this patch, and should that change go in as its own patch with a release note?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The one existing command it names, `alter foreign table ... rename column`, already reports ALTER FOREIGN TABLE today.

touch_points.reason: The patch adds a non-standard `alter foreign table ... rename constraint` form in gram.y.

touch_points.reason: The patch extends tab completion for alter foreign table rename constraint and add/drop column/constraint.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch refactors AlterObjectTypeCommandTag() in tcop/utility.c and adds a second spelling to keep documented and tested.

touch_points.reason: Message #1 says `alter table ... rename constraint` already does this on foreign tables.

questions: Why is a cross-reference to `alter table ... rename constraint` in the alter foreign table documentation not enough?
Does any existing statement return a different command tag after the AlterObjectTypeCommandTag() refactor, and if so, which?
Which constraint types on a foreign table can the new form rename?
How do `only` and `*` behave when the renamed constraint is inherited by or from another table?
Do the regression tests check the command tag returned for the new form and for the existing column and constraint forms?

committability.liability: One more grammar form to keep in step with alter table, and the refactored command tag logic, which event triggers and clients depend on, for as long as the syntax exists.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the thread has only the first message.

provisional_note: Without the code, the scope of the AlterObjectTypeCommandTag() refactor cannot be checked, so the claim that no existing command changes its tag is unverified. The behaviour of `only` and `*` for inherited constraints also could not be judged.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PROPOSAL] : Disallow use of empty column name in (column_name '') in ALTER or CREATE of foreign table.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes postgres_fdw's validator reject empty values for the column_name, schema_name and table_name options in create or alter foreign table. Today an empty column_name is accepted, and the remote query then fails with a zero-length identifier error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane judged that the check did not add enough ease-of-use to justify the extra code, and he compared an empty name to a misspelled remote name, which cannot be checked either. Robert Haas pointed out that existing foreign tables with empty values would then fail pg_dump or pg_upgrade. Nobody argued for the patch after Tom voted against it, so Robert marked it Rejected.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I was down on it to start with, on the grounds that it wasn't adding enough ease-of-use to justify even a relatively small amount of added code.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_get_constraintdef schema-qualify the referenced table in a foreign key's REFERENCES clause when pretty printing is off, as pg_get_indexdef already does. The goal is constraint definitions that can be recreated on another system with a different search_path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said pg_get_indexdef is the odd one out, since most generate_relation_name calls in ruleutils.c ignore the pretty flag, and Alvaro Herrera judged the patch too small for making PRETTYFLAG_SCHEMA work consistently. Tom asked for a clearly defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper function. The author did not reply to these reviews, and Michael Paquier returned the patch after six weeks without a reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In other words, I think your patch is too small.

precedents_retrieved.title: TRUNCATE on foreign tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an optional ExecForeignTruncate callback to FdwRoutine so that TRUNCATE works on foreign tables, including foreign partitions of a partitioned table. The callback gets the foreign tables of one server as a list, with DropBehavior and restart_seqs, and postgres_fdw sends one remote TRUNCATE for them.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback because the implementation, the docs and the tests needed more work. The open issues at that point were ONLY handling, since TRUNCATE ONLY on a local foreign table could truncate the whole inheritance tree on the remote server, and a possible separate truncatable option for postgres_fdw. Missing postgres_fdw documentation and missing inheritance tests were also still open.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: For now, as the patch needs more work for its implementation, docs and tests, I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change a constraint's index - ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX ...
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. Alvaro Herrera and Laurenz Albe agreed that primary keys with INCLUDE columns would first need PRIMARY KEY syntax, so that pg_dump works. That leaves this command a narrow use case. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TBH I think if we really wanted the feature of primary keys with
included columns, we'd have to add it to the PRIMARY KEY syntax rather
than having an ad-hoc ALTER TABLE ALTER CONSTRAINT USING INDEX command
to replace the index underneath.

precedents_retrieved.title: alter table set TABLE ACCESS METHOD
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an ALTER TABLE ... SET TABLE ACCESS METHOD command that rewrites a table into a different table access method, so data can be migrated between AMs without manually recreating the table. The patch also detoasted tuples in ATRewriteTable during the rewrite so that the new AM would not receive data compressed or toasted by the old one.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last messages show reviewers agreeing that the detoasting step in ATRewriteTable could be removed because detoasting is the table AM's responsibility, and discussing whether a dummy table AM test module would be useful; none of them gives a reason for withdrawing the entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: CHECK constraint deferrable Support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets CHECK constraints be declared DEFERRABLE and INITIALLY DEFERRED, as the SQL standard allows, so SET CONSTRAINTS can delay a CHECK until commit. Rows that fail a deferrable CHECK are rechecked at commit time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the CHECK implementation assumes constraints are immutable, and the patch does not change that assumption, so he called the feature a toy. Others then argued it should be dropped or combined with deferrable NOT NULL, which Robert Haas and Vik Fearing disputed. Dean Rasheed also reported open bugs, including a deferred constraint that still failed immediately and a wrong constraint-exclusion result. The visible messages do not show why the author withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I continue to assert that basing this feature on the current CHECK implementation will produce nothing but a toy feature, that's not only of little practical use but will be an active foot-gun for people who expect it to do more than it can.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P1] is about postgres_fdw rejecting empty option values, which is a different idea. Its cost-versus-ease-of-use reason does not carry over to a small grammar addition that reuses an existing rename path. Message #1 points to no earlier discussion of this idea, so the prior-attempts angle gives no basis for an objection.

The new syntax copies alter table rename constraint, adds no keyword, and needs no pg_dump change, because constraint names are already dumped. The only compatibility concern I found is the command tag side effect.
Apart from the command tag, the patch adds no persistent or cross-node state. It adds a grammar form and reuses the existing rename path, so there is no catalog, WAL, on-disk or ABI change.

The proposal adds a grammar alias for an operation that alter table ... rename constraint already performs on foreign tables, so it lets no one do anything new. Ownership checks and locking come from the existing rename path. The command tag change could matter to event triggers that filter on tags, but that is a compatibility question for another angle.

The new syntax itself carries little long-run cost: it reuses the existing rename path, adds no catalog, GUC or hot-path work, and matches the existing rename column form. [P1] was rejected for low value per line of code, but here the code is small and the form fits existing grammar, so it is not cited.
One fixable objection only. The consistency argument for the new syntax is reasonable, so this is a question of value against cost, not a reason to reject.

Demand is thin: one user, self-described as niche, and alter table ... rename constraint already works on foreign tables. Still, the cost is one grammar form, one doc line and tab completion, and ten such consistency fixes per release would be acceptable. The command tag change is for the design angle to judge.
